newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Firmer on crude, swaps.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Firmer on crude, swaps.

text.p: Singapore middle-distillate prices were firmer on the back of a rise in crude and swaps values, traders said on Monday.
Swaps for August gained 40 cents to be last quoted at $21.35/$21.45 per barrel, while September rose by 15 cents to be last quoted at $22.10/$22.30.
A rally on gas oil futures prices to $164.50 per tonne, up $2.50 also helped boost sentiment in Asia which was nevertheless still dampened by poor demand as China remained at bay.

Traders said if the news of tight physical supplies in northwest Europe were to result in buyers there seeking supplies elsewhere which meet their strict requirements, supplies from Asia could also be working their way to Europe.
Asian gas oil has already started to make their way to two South American countries, but the firmer levels on Monday might make it more difficult to ship cargoes westwards.
A European major on Monday offered two cargoes--July 29-August 2 at $152 per tonne ($20.40 per barrel) and August 9-13 at $156 ($20.95 per barrel), with no bids seen.
This was higher than the $148.50 per tonne ($19.93 per barrel) and $20.00 it offered on Friday.
Other offers were seen for August 3-7 at $20.85 per barrel.
China was said to have bought last week at $153-$154 per tonne, cost-and-freight basis.
India bought by tender one kerosene cargo for August delivery from Mobil at three cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f Indian east coast.
